questions.q: In the fraction 3/4, what do the numbers 3 and 4 represent?
questions.a: 3 is the numerator (parts we have) and 4 is the denominator (total equal parts). If a student says 3 is the top and 4 is the bottom, they recall the position but not the meaning; if they flip them, they misunderstand the core concept of a share.

questions.q: If you divide a chocolate bar into 5 parts, but they are all different sizes, can you say one piece is 1/5 of the bar? Why or why not?
questions.a: No, because fractions require equal parts. If the pieces are different sizes, they are not "equal shares," and therefore we cannot use a single fraction to describe a part of that whole.

questions.q: You have 1 kg of apples and divide them into 4 equal bags. What fraction of the total weight is in one bag?
questions.a: The fraction is 1/4. We identify the whole (1 kg) and divide by the number of equal parts (4). Answering 4/1 shows the student has reversed the numerator and denominator, which is a common error.

questions.q: If you have 1/6 of a cake and your friend has 1/3 of the same cake, who has a larger piece? Explain why.
questions.a: The friend with 1/3 has a larger piece. Because 1/3 means the cake is cut into only 3 big pieces, while 1/6 means it is cut into 6 smaller pieces; dividing a whole into more parts makes each part smaller.

questions.q: Is it possible to have a fraction like 5/0? Why or why not?
questions.a: No, the denominator cannot be zero because you cannot divide a whole into zero parts. Division by zero is undefined, and a fraction represents an actual division of a physical or numerical whole.

questions.q: Draw a square. Show how you would shade 3/4 of it. If you had to create a different shape representing 3/4, how would you change your approach?
questions.a: The student should divide the square into 4 equal parts and shade 3. For a different shape (like a circle), they must still ensure 4 equal parts are created. Poor answers fail to keep the parts equal in size.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: A fraction ______ a part of a whole, where a single object or a collection is divided into equal shares.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you have one delicious paratha and you want to share it ______ with your best friend.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to identify, write, and draw fractions given a real-world sharing scenario, and correctly label the numerator and denominator.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Imagine you have one ______ paratha and you want to share it equally with your best friend.
